sun_events — DRIVE env op

• Data kinds: scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sun_events(year: 'int', month: 'int', day: 'int', lat: 'float', lon: 'float', tz_hours: 'float' = 9.0, *, h0: 'float' = -0.8333) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import driveenv; driveenv.sun_events(year: 'int', month: 'int', day: 'int', lat: 'float', lon: 'float', tz_hours: 'float' = 9.0, *, h0: 'float' = -0.8333) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("sun_events"))

Usage

Times of sunrise, solar noon and sunset for the day (local calendar date), plus the azimuths of sunrise/sunset and the altitude at solar noon.

Sunset = geometric altitude of the center of the sun is h0 (default −0.8333° = atmospheric difference 34′ + visual radius 16′, top side touches the horizon) Time to cross. h0="naoj" is the definition of the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan's Ephemeris Computation Office (the upper side of the sun is the visual horizon, the horizontal atmospheric difference is 35'8'', and the visual radius is from the distance). South middle = hour angle 0. Both solve sun_at for time (bisection method, interval width less than 1e-7 days ≈ up to 0.009 seconds).

Returns

dict: sunrise / transit / sunset (datetime with time zone, None if there is no sunrise or sunset), sunrise_azimuth / sunset_azimuth(degrees), transit_altitude(degrees, geometric altitude without atmospheric difference and transit_altitude_apparent).
